title: The Neutronium Alchemist
author: Hamilton, Peter F.
review:
Honestly sort of struggled with this one. It also feels like such a middle book where the beginning is a lot of climax and falling action before introducing the main drive for this book. And nothing is really resolved after 1200 pages which can feel a bit unrewarding even though there's a lot of good stuff in between.

The main plot point I did struggle to get motivated by or at least the moment to moment parts were less interesting than the first book, but the drives behind it and the potential consequences are very high.

The horror elements felt a lot less prevalent here as well which I sort of view as a negative since I really enjoyed that in the first book and was missing those here.

The amount of plot lines and the complexity of the world and events almost hit a breaking point for me, but it barely holds things together here and we do get some really good moments and some of the characters we've been interacting with have interesting and high consequence things to do.

There's also a lot of complexity in the motivations and the different factions where even the main protagonist and antagonist factions have many different sub factions who have different motivations and objectives.

Overall this is a lot of book and can feel overwhelming a lot of times but it's also really good and so much is left unanswered that I do want to know how PFH wraps it all up.

Pretty impressed as well how this maintains the brand of big bold and unforgiving science fiction but in a drastically different way from the previous book. Makes it easy to respect the sheer will and ambition of the series even though it can feel like drowning at times.

Will take a bit of a breather before I slowly digest the last book and see what's in store for this crazy universe this man has crafted.
